scope: Independent full-source audit of targets DCP-LETT-1894, 1897, 2151, 2177F and context 1794. Existing canonical report is preserved; no primary notes, decisions, ledgers or exports changed.

record_reviews.source_kind: Darwin ALS, complete surviving 7-paragraph body with apparatus and bibliography
record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Layard for a valuable earlier letter and hopes Layard will pursue Madagascar domestic-animal information. He asks about fertility of hybrid cats, possible native dog/wild-dog crosses, and whether promiscuously crossed dog populations become uniform. He then asks Layard to put two specific questions to Fry: Ascension feral-pigeon coloration and an alleged North African short curled-tailed greyhound. He requests Cape pigeon, duck and poultry specimens, explains his skeleton-based comparison of slight breed differences, and asks about a general sea-fowl synopsis in response to Layard’s question. The letter is Darwin-authored throughout; no incoming Layard text is embedded.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 8 June [1856], XML single day 1856-06-08; bracketed year is editorially supplied, while composition, dispatch and Layard receipt remain distinct.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Charles Darwin body voice; references to Lichtenstein, Fry, Andersson and monuments are reported sources, not their voices.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Darwin letter of 9 December 1855 to Layard starts a domestic-breed/Cape information thread, but 1894 explicitly thanks a separate intervening valuable letter and cannot be treated as a direct reply to 1794 without the missing intervening Layard source.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Outgoing request; its likely immediate Layard antecedent is not preserved.

evidence.quote: Firstly I do hope that you will try & discover whether the hybrid Cats are fertile; I fear that this wd. be very difficult inter se; but with either parent you cannot fail to discover. Secondly Licktenstein asserts that the natives have a breed of domestic dogs like the C. mesomelas

Fourthly would you kindly take the trouble to ask Mr. Fry two questions; whether, if he can remember, the feral Pigeons at Ascension, had black bars on wing & white rumps, or whether they were chequered like common Dove cot.

record_reviews.source_kind: Incomplete Layard incoming letter; surviving 5 paragraphs, apparatus, annotations and bibliography read in full
record_reviews.summary: Layard reports a local discussion with Fry about hereditary “impression” from an earlier sire: a horse’s first foal was by a jackass, and the horse and its sister later proved to share that maternal history. Layard adds his own observations of bitches repeatedly producing offspring resembling a former mate. Fry claims stallions prefer mule mares, jackasses mule mares, and drakes hybrid Muscovies; Layard presents this as local report, not tested fact. Fry cannot identify Ascension pigeon coloration because he did not distinguish pigeon types. He has seen a greyhound-like Caffre dog with a slightly bushed curled tail and plans further inquiries while describing a possible judicial circuit. The surviving body ends mid-sentence (“I literally dare not read a book of Travels,—I cannot”), so the physical letter is incomplete even though all available text was read.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [September–October 1856], XML bounded 1856-09-01 through 1856-10-31; exact order/date and receipt are unresolved. Editorial dating assumes a reply to Darwin’s 8 June letter arriving in Cape Town in late August or early September, not documentary proof of a precise day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Layard is the surviving author; Fry’s claims and observations are explicitly reported within Layard’s prose. Darwin annotations are separate pencil layers and do not alter authorship.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1794 asks Layard for Cape pigeon and domestic-breed evidence in 1855; 1897’s exact Ascension and greyhound answers instead track the specific questions in 1894 P4, while the missing 1794-to-1894 correspondence prevents using 1794 as the immediate antecedent.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Strong partial reply to 1894 P4: exact Ascension and greyhound prompts are answered, while the rest of 1894’s cat/dog/Cape requests are not fully answered or remain prospective.

evidence.quote: Fry never was accustomed to distinguish between the Pigeons, till I pointed out to him the Differences between them, & therefore cannot remember if the Ascension birds had black bars on the Wings, & white rumps, he calls them “Blue rocks”.
Respecting the Greyhound with “very short and much curled tail”, Fry says, he has seen a dog of the greyhound kind among the caffres, with a curled tail slightly bushed.

record_reviews.source_kind: Darwin ALS with separately transcribed five-question enclosure, apparatus and bibliography
record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Buckman to trace the Cirencester source of a rare “Smiter” pigeon bought through Roe and to have that person answer five enclosed questions about provenance, habits, cage display, sex differences, and breeding true in form and colour. He offers Holland as an alternative intermediary if Buckman cannot help. The final two paragraphs ask when Buckman’s British Association plant-variation report will be published and request references to his earlier work, explaining Darwin’s interest in cultivation-driven variation. The enclosure is a distinct scholarly section and must not be merged into the body.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 4 October [1857], XML single day 1857-10-04; supplied year retained, with no receipt date inferred.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin authored body and enclosure questions; Buckman’s reported paper and Bentham reference are editorial/contextual references, not embedded Buckman voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same correspondent and one-day interval are insufficient: 2177F has no surviving transcript and its catalogue summary concerns native/foreign weeds, with no demonstrated Smiters or enclosure response.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Outgoing request with a missing Buckman response and missing/undemonstrated enclosure outcome; no supported incoming antecedent in this packet.

evidence.quote: Now would you be so very kind as to endeavour to find out the gentleman & beg him to answer the questions on the enclosed paper.
I have lately seen a short abstract in Athenæum of a communication by you on the variation of Plants by culture read before Brit. Assoc.

record_reviews.source_kind: Incomplete incoming record with no online body transcription
record_reviews.summary: The preserved DCP page explicitly states that the transcript is not yet available online; only the summary “Discusses the relative growth of native and foreign weeds” survives. No historical body, enclosure, authorial argument or reply scope can be reconstructed from this record.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [1 December 1857], XML single day 1857-12-01; bracketed date is retained, but no physical receipt or exact composition evidence is available here.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Metadata attributes the unavailable record to James Buckman; no surviving prose is available to test voice or reported material.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same Buckman correspondent, but the only available 2177F summary is about weeds and cannot demonstrate a response to the Smiter-pigeon request or plant-publication questions in 2151.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Body unavailable; catalogue summary alone cannot establish a reply or contemporary content.

record_reviews.source_kind: Darwin ALS, complete surviving 8-paragraph body with apparatus and bibliography; prior-period context
record_reviews.summary: Darwin introduces himself to Layard after reading several Ceylon natural-history communications, explains his long-term variation/origin-of-species project, and concentrates on domestic pigeons, poultry, ducks and rabbits. He asks Layard to obtain Cape-bred pigeon, duck and poultry specimens or skins, and asks for information on cattle and dogs kept by western-coast tribes; Andersson is separately named as a promised source. A postscript asks about pigeon fanciers in Ceylon and whether two named shell species occur there, reporting Benson’s doubt about Layard’s authority. This is an earlier Darwin-originating request and context for the Layard thread, not a surviving incoming response to 1894.
record_reviews.date_assessment: 9 December 1855, XML single day 1855-12-09; outside the 1856–57 period and retained only as contextual predecessor.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin body voice; Andersson, Benson, Thwaites and the cited works are reported or editorially referenced.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: 1894 continues the Layard domestic-animal/Cape inquiry but explicitly thanks an intervening Layard letter; with that immediate input missing, 1794 should be referenced as an earlier thread origin rather than paired as the direct antecedent.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context only; no direct reply edge proposed.

evidence.quote: For various reasons, I have determined to work especially on pigeons, poultry, ducks & rabbits; though at the same time I am most grateful for any facts on all our other domesticated quadrupeds & birds.

Now would you confer the very great favour on me to make enquiries for me on this head; & I have thought that you might employ any bird-skinner (if such exist) at my expence, to look out for & skin old examples dying a natural death of any breed whatever

proposed_links.reason: 1897 P4 answers the distinctive Ascension pigeon question from 1894 P4, and 1897 P5 answers the distinctive short, curled-tailed greyhound question from the same paragraph. The response is partial: cat, dog-cross uniformity, Cape pigeon specimen, duck and poultry requests are not all answered; the telegony and mule material is Layard/Fry reporting, not assumed to answer an unlocated prompt.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1897 P4–P5 only; 1897 P1–P3 remain separate reported material unless independently matched.

unlocated_references.description: Immediate earlier Layard letter thanked in P1 is not preserved; 1897 is the surviving partial response.
Buckman’s response and the outcome of the five-question Smiter enclosure are not present; 2177F cannot fill this gap because its body is unavailable and summary concerns weeds.

issues: Canonical batch-26 summaries use opening/closing fragments and should not be treated as substantive evidence.
1897 is physically incomplete and ends mid-sentence; all surviving text was read, but unavailable continuation must remain held.
2177F has no surviving body transcription; its summary cannot establish a reply to 2151.
1894→1897 linkage must use response→antecedent direction (1897 replies_to 1894) and only the directly answered P4 questions.
